verifiable-quality-gates.why: each new CLI behavior is pinned by a test that FAILS if reverted: --help exits 0 with usage, and a typo'd flag exits 2 (not silently ignored) on esk-init/esk-genesis/check-skill-receipt/claim-lint (#140)
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added 8 ISSUE-140 discrimination cases across the four test files; full suite 760 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

architectural-decision-records.why: rejecting an unknown flag is a small CLI-contract change (an undocumented flag now errors instead of being ignored), recorded in one ADR
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0081 covering --help + unknown-flag rejection and the honest limits (--prefixed only; positional/single-dash unchanged)
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: pinned at the level that owns it: each tool is spawned with --help and with a typo'd flag and its real exit code + output are asserted
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: spawn-based help/unknown-flag tests for all four CLIs
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug, and match the test type to the risk.

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the non-happy paths were enumerated and committed: a help request, and a misspelled flag (the --persnal footgun) for each tool
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: node:test cases asserting --help exit 0 + usage and unknown-flag exit 2 + message
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

skeptical-audit.why: ADR-0081 states the honest limits rather than overclaiming: the guard inspects --prefixed args only, positional + single-dash are unchanged by design, and the usage text is a summary not a full reference
skeptical-audit.what: recorded the limits in ADR-0081 and verified the full suite + the receipt gate's own self-check green before claiming the fix
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review was run on the four-CLI delta before the PR, checking the known-flag sets are complete (no real flag rejected) and the guard cannot flag an option value
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch in a fresh subagent and recorded it in the arch-review log
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the unknown-flag rejection is CLI argument hygiene (a typo can't silently change scope), covered by the discrimination tests; no product input/auth/crypto surface changed that would take an @security scenario

pattern-selector.why: no new feature, class, module or data flow; a help/guard block added to each CLI's existing arg parse

arch-encode.why: enforced by discrimination tests, not a new rules-file entry

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no PII, retention, migration or audit logic; CLI ergonomics

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system, service, database or integration architecture changed

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature-flag or rollback mechanism; CLI tooling

sre-operational-readiness.why: no SLI/SLO, alert, runbook or production-operability surface

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no graphical or web UI; developer-facing command-line tooling

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or frontend code; command-line tooling

usability-ux-universal-design.why: developer-facing CLI, not an end-user flow/screen/form; the --help text and clear error messages are the usability improvement this PR makes, but there is no UI surface the skill governs
